questions.q:
The UN General Assembly declared 2026 the International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists. Consider the following statements:
1. The observance is led by the Food and Agriculture Organization.
2. Grasslands cover about 24% of India's geographical area, with less than 1% under formal conservation.
3. Banni Grassland, described as Asia's largest, is in Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Banni Grassland is in Kutch, Gujarat, so 3 is wrong. Grasslands are the least protected of India's major ecosystems because they are often classed as 'wastelands', which is why the Year puts the spotlight on pastoralist livelihoods and rangeland conservation.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Ecologist Madhav Gadgil, who chaired the Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel (WGEEP) set up in 2010, had recommended that the entire Western Ghats be declared an Ecologically Sensitive Area in three zones.
Statement-II: The government implemented the WGEEP recommendations without any change.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The 2011 WGEEP report proposed an ESA for the whole range, but the government instead followed the Kasturirangan High-Level Working Group (2013), which proposed an ESA of 56,825 sq km only. Gadgil, who founded IISc's Centre for Ecological Sciences in 1982, died in Pune aged 83 in January 2026.

questions.q:
A forest fire burned for five days in the Valley of Flowers National Park in January 2026, and Uttarakhand sought help from the Indian Air Force. Consider the following statements:
1. It was declared a national park in 1982.
2. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005.
3. It forms a core zone of the Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve.
4. It lies in Pithoragarh district.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 to 3 are correct. The park is in Chamoli district, not Pithoragarh, and was discovered in 1931 by the mountaineer Frank Smythe.

questions.q: The UNEP report 'State of Finance for Nature 2026' found that nature-negative financial flows reached USD 7.3 trillion in 2023. Which one of the following is consistent with its findings?
o: Nature-negative flows were about USD 3 for every USD 1 invested in protecting nature
Nature-negative flows were about USD 30 for every USD 1 invested in protecting nature
Investment in nature-based solutions of USD 571 billion a year already exceeds the need of USD 220 billion
Governments provide almost no subsidies that are harmful to the environment
questions.e: Nature-based solutions investment stood at USD 220 billion against a need of USD 571 billion a year by 2030, so the gap is large; governments also provide about USD 2.4 trillion in environmentally harmful subsidies. The report therefore argues for redirecting existing finance rather than only raising new money.

questions.q:
Match the animal reported in the news in January 2026 (List-I) with the place associated with it (List-II):
List-I: A. Eastern Imperial Eagle (confirmed in winter)  B. Indian bison (population rise)  C. Indian Skimmer (sighted after nearly 20 years)  D. Irrawaddy dolphin (main Indian habitat)
List-II: 1. Mudumalai Tiger Reserve  2. Debrigarh Wildlife Sanctuary  3. Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary  4. Chilika Lake
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The Eastern Imperial Eagle (IUCN Vulnerable) was confirmed at Mudumalai in Tamil Nadu, the gaur count in Debrigarh (Bargarh, Odisha) rose by 189 to 848, and the Endangered Indian Skimmer was seen along 60 km of the Ganga in Bhagalpur, Bihar. The euryhaline Irrawaddy dolphin (Endangered) occurs in India mainly in Chilika Lake.

questions.q:
The Expert Appraisal Committee recommended a major design overhaul of the proposed International Dugong Conservation Centre at Manora, Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu. Consider the following statements:
1. The site lies in a CRZ-III No Development Zone and overlaps mangroves and seagrass.
2. The dugong is listed Vulnerable by the IUCN and is in Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.
3. The dugong is a freshwater mammal that feeds mainly on mangrove leaves.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The dugong is a marine mammal that grazes on seagrass, which is why the Gulf of Mannar and Palk Bay seagrass meadows (over 13 species) are its key habitat in India; mangrove leaves are not its diet. It is also in CITES Appendix I.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about species in the news:
1. The Eastern Imperial Eagle (IUCN Vulnerable) was confirmed at Mudumalai Tiger Reserve during the winter migratory season.
2. Phayre's leaf monkey, listed Endangered, is found mainly in Tripura, Assam and Mizoram.
3. The gaur, whose population in Debrigarh Wildlife Sanctuary rose to 848, is listed Endangered by the IUCN.
4. Brandt's hedgehog, newly recorded in India from Jammu and Kashmir, is listed Least Concern by the IUCN.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The gaur is listed Vulnerable by the IUCN (and is in CITES Appendix I and Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972). Brandt's hedgehog is a desert species also found in Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan, which is why its record from J&K was confirmed by DNA analysis.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Aralam Wildlife Sanctuary, renamed Aralam Butterfly Sanctuary on 11 January 2026 as Kerala's first butterfly sanctuary, is in Wayanad district.
2. Aralam borders Karnataka's Brahmagiri Wildlife Sanctuary.
3. Kerala declared Bacillus subtilis, a spore-forming Gram-positive bacterium, its State microbe.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Aralam is in Kannur district, so 1 is wrong. It has over 266 butterfly species (more than 80% of Kerala's) and is also a habitat of the Schedule I slender loris. Bacillus subtilis is a soil and gut probiotic bacterium used as a fungicide.

questions.q:
The Prime Minister laid the foundation stone of the Kaziranga Elevated Corridor in Assam, and the Assam government completed an eviction drive in Burhachapori Wildlife Sanctuary. Consider the following statements:
1. The corridor is a 34.5 km elevated wildlife-friendly section of the four-laning of the Kaliabor-Numaligarh stretch of NH-715.
2. Burhachapori Wildlife Sanctuary lies on the north bank of the Brahmaputra.
3. Kaziranga is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and has the world's largest population of one-horned rhinoceroses.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Burhachapori, in Sonitpur district, lies on the south bank of the Brahmaputra, forms the Laokhowa-Burhachapori ecosystem and was notified as a buffer zone of Kaziranga Tiger Reserve in 2007. An elevated corridor lets animals cross beneath the highway, reducing road kills during Brahmaputra floods.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, 19 Jan 2026; Vajiram & Ravi, 8 Jan 2026

questions.q:
The Environment Ministry notified the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 in January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. They are notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, supersede the 2016 Rules and take effect on 1 April 2026.
2. They require segregation at source into only two streams, wet and dry.
3. They introduce Extended Bulk Waste Generator Responsibility.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Rules require four-stream segregation: wet, dry, sanitary and special care waste. They also add environmental compensation for non-compliance and raise the use of refuse-derived fuel (RDF) by cement and waste-to-energy plants from 5% to 15% over six years.

questions.q:
The first phase of the All-India Tiger Estimation 2026 began at Thanthai Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary in Erode, Tamil Nadu. Consider the following statements:
1. The estimation is conducted every five years.
2. Field staff use the M-STrIPES app, launched in 2010 by the National Tiger Conservation Authority and the Wildlife Institute of India.
3. Madhya Pradesh announced that the Ratapani Tiger Reserve, which contains the Bhimbetka rock shelters, will be named after Dr Vishnu Shridhar Wakankar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The estimation is a four-year cycle (2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022 and now 2026, the sixth cycle). Ratapani lies in Raisen and Sehore districts in the Vindhya ranges north of the Narmada.

questions.q:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah laid the foundation stone in Gandhinagar for India's first State-funded BSL-4 laboratory. Consider the following statements:
1. It will be run by the Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre under the Gujarat State Biotechnology Mission.
2. BSL-4 is the lowest biosafety level, meant for pathogens that pose little risk to laboratory staff.
3. The National Institute of Virology, Pune hosts India's other civilian BSL-4 laboratory.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: BSL-4 is the highest biosafety level, used for dangerous pathogens with no easy cure or vaccine, such as Ebola, Nipah, Marburg, CCHF and Kyasanur Forest Disease, which the Gandhinagar lab plans to study. It will be India's second civilian BSL-4 lab after NIV Pune.

questions.q: MeitY demonstrated 'Shrutlekh' in January 2026. Which one of the following best describes it?
o: An AI tool under BHASHINI for real-time multilingual speech-to-text translation of speeches
A Sanskrit-only optical character recognition tool for manuscripts run by the Archaeological Survey of India
A voice assistant for UPI payments developed by the National Payments Corporation of India
A blockchain tool for translating land records, developed by the National Informatics Centre
questions.e: BHASHINI operates under the National Language Translation Mission, supports 22 scheduled languages and includes the Bhashadaan crowdsourcing initiative to gather language data. Shrutlekh applies it to speech, converting spoken words into text in other languages in real time.

questions.q:
The Union government released draft guidelines for a Battery Pack Aadhaar system. Consider the following statements:
1. Every battery pack gets a 12-digit Battery Pack Aadhaar Number (BPAN).
2. Static data such as manufacturer, specifications and carbon footprint is stored on the BPAN, while dynamic data such as battery health and charge cycles sits on a central server.
3. It applies to every electric-vehicle battery pack and industrial battery above 2 kWh, with a QR code for lifecycle traceability.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The BPAN is a 21-character identifier, not 12 digits, and the QR code allows traceability across the battery's life, from manufacture to recycling. This supports battery reuse and recycling and reduces the risk of unsafe or counterfeit packs.

questions.q:
The Department of Telecommunications de-licensed the lower half of the 6 GHz band for indoor use in January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The de-licensed band is 5,925-6,425 MHz, enabling Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7.
2. Its use is prohibited on moving vehicles and oil rigs.
3. De-licensing means the spectrum will be auctioned to telecom operators for exclusive use.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: De-licensed spectrum can be used by anyone without a licence or auction, which is why it suits Wi-Fi; auctions apply to licensed, exclusive spectrum such as mobile bands. The restriction on vehicles and oil rigs prevents interference with other services.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Menkes disease, for which the US FDA approved Zycubo (copper histidinate) in January 2026, mostly affects male infants.
Statement-II: It is caused by a mutation in the ATP7A gene on the X chromosome, which impairs copper transport.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Because the gene lies on the X chromosome, the disorder is X-linked recessive: a male has only one X and so a single faulty copy causes disease, while females usually have a second, working copy. Zycubo is the first treatment approved for Menkes disease in paediatric patients.
questions.h: Boys have one X: one faulty ATP7A is enough

questions.q:
ISRO's PSLV-C62 failed on 12 January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The mission carried the EOS-N1 (Anvesha) Earth observation satellite and 15 co-passenger satellites, all of which were lost.
2. It was the second PSLV failure in a row, after PSLV-C61 in May 2025, both linked to a third-stage anomaly.
3. The anomaly occurred in the liquid-fuelled second stage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The PSLV has four stages that alternate solid (PS1), liquid (PS2), solid (PS3) and liquid (PS4); the anomaly was in the solid third stage, PS3, where the vehicle lost stability near burnout. PSLV-C61 had carried EOS-09, and ISRO's Chairman V. Narayanan said the cause was under analysis.

questions.q:
A rare blood-red auroral display was captured by the all-sky camera at the Indian Astronomical Observatory, Hanle, in Ladakh. Consider the following statements:
1. Hanle lies in the Changthang region at about 4,500 m and hosts a Dark Sky Reserve.
2. It is India's first International Dark Sky Reserve and is managed by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics under the Department of Science and Technology.
3. The Reserve was notified in December 2022 by the Ministry of Defence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Reserve was notified in December 2022 by the Ladakh administration, not the Ministry of Defence. Its high altitude, dry air and low light pollution make it suitable for astronomy and for observing rare auroral emissions.

questions.q: ISRO's Chairman V. Narayanan spoke about the Gaganyaan programme on 30 January 2026. Which one of the following was his statement?
o: The crewed flight will be undertaken in 2026 after a single uncrewed mission
The programme will be replaced by the Bharatiya Antariksh Station and no crewed flight to low Earth orbit is planned
The Gaganyaan crewed programme is planned for 2027, with three uncrewed missions preceding the crewed flight
Five uncrewed missions will be flown before a crewed flight in 2030
questions.e: The uncrewed missions are meant to test the crew module, life-support and recovery before astronauts (Gaganyatris) fly. The announcement came weeks after the PSLV-C62 failure, which highlights the reliability pressure on India's launch programme.

questions.q:
DRDO completed user evaluation trials of the Akash-NG surface-to-air missile with the Indian Air Force as the user. Consider the following statements:
1. Akash-NG has a range of up to 70 km, against about 30 km for the original Akash.
2. It has about 96% indigenous content, with Bharat Dynamics and Bharat Electronics as production partners.
3. Like the original Akash, it uses a ramjet propulsion system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The original Akash is ramjet-propelled, but Akash-NG uses a solid rocket motor and flies at Mach 2.5. The change gives better manoeuvrability and a longer engagement range.

questions.q: DRDO and the Indian Army conducted successful trials of the Man Portable Anti-tank Guided Missile (MPATGM). Which one of the following correctly describes it?
o: A first-generation wire-guided missile that the operator steers to the target
A shoulder-fired surface-to-air missile for engaging low-flying aircraft
A ship-launched anti-ship missile with a range of 1,500 km
A third-generation fire-and-forget missile with an imaging infrared seeker for day-and-night capability and a tandem warhead
questions.e: Fire-and-forget means the missile locks on to the target and needs no further guidance from the operator, who can move away after firing. The tandem warhead defeats armour fitted with explosive reactive protection, and Bharat Dynamics and Bharat Electronics are the production partners.

questions.q:
Match List-I (naval/coast guard vessel) with List-II (description):
List-I: A. ICGS Samudra Pratap  B. INSV Kaundinya  C. INS Sudarshini  D. INS Sagardhwani
List-II: 1. Sail training ship on the Lokayan 26 expedition  2. India's first 'stitched ship', built with the ancient Tankai method  3. First of two indigenous pollution control vessels built by Goa Shipyard Limited  4. Ship flagged off for the fifth Sagar Maitri mission, a joint Navy-DRDO programme
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: ICGS Samudra Pratap, homeported at Kochi, is the largest Coast Guard vessel; INSV Kaundinya sailed from Porbandar to Muscat; INS Sudarshini began its 10-month Lokayan 26 voyage on 20 January 2026; and INS Sagardhwani (SM-5) retraces INS Kistna's route in the 1962-65 International Indian Ocean Expedition.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, 7, 22 and 24 Jan 2026; Vajiram & Ravi, 20 Jan 2026

questions.q:
The 78th Army Day was observed on 15 January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. It was the first Army Day parade held outside a cantonment, in Jaipur.
2. Army Day marks the day Field Marshal Sam Manekshaw took over as Chief of the Army Staff.
3. The new Bhairav Battalions made their debut, and the Army named 2026 the 'Year of Networking and Data Centricity'.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Army Day marks 15 January 1949, when Field Marshal K.M. Cariappa became the first Indian Commander-in-Chief, taking over from the last British chief. Each Bhairav battalion has about 200-250 personnel drawn from infantry, artillery, air defence and signals.

questions.q:
The 77th Republic Day parade on 26 January 2026 was held at Kartavya Path. Consider the following statements:
1. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa were the chief guests.
2. DRDO's Long Range Anti-Ship Hypersonic Missile (LR-AShM), a hypersonic glide missile, was showcased for the first time.
3. The parade's theme was '150 Years of Jana Gana Mana'.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The parade theme was '150 Years of Vande Mataram', so 3 is wrong. The LR-AShM is a glide missile with a range of about 1,500 km and speeds up to Mach 10, using a two-stage solid rocket motor, and the India-EU FTA conclusion was announced the next day.
questions.s: The Statesman, 26 Jan 2026; Vajiram & Ravi, 9 Jan 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about internal security measures in January 2026:
1. The National IED Data Management System (NIDMS), launched on 9 January 2026, was developed by the National Security Guard's National Bomb Data Centre.
2. NIDMS is a one-way repository maintained by the National Investigation Agency alone.
3. NATGRID, conceived in 2009 after the 26/11 attacks, was integrated with the National Population Register.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NIDMS is a two-way platform where the NIA, Anti-Terrorism Squads, State police and Central Armed Police Forces can upload and analyse IED incident data; the NSG has kept a bomb-blast database since 1999. NATGRID became operational in 2023 and the NPR integration gives authorised agencies family-level data of about 119 crore residents.
questions.s: All India Radio News, 9 Jan 2026; Drishti IAS, 3 Jan 2026
